purpose: Test actuator-aware whole-body action ordering in 165 fresh worlds with the unchanged repeated-action comparisons.
code_path_risks_covered: Fresh prepared torso and limb contacts remain bound to cell, morphology, model and canonical state
Exact model identities and schedules plus declared unit-specific bounds match every prepared prefix without state restoration
Contact multisets match exact geometry pairs with bounded positions, gaps and frames, independently of enumeration
Each of nine bounded alternatives has two fresh worlds at each of three intervention times on all three exposed shapes
All measured and predicted scores project onto the primary action-zero repeat-zero prepared axis
Each repeated-action spread and prediction interval must stay at or below 1e-5 rad/s; ambiguous measured pairs need the unchanged 1e-4 rad/s separation
Only disjoint prediction intervals earn correct ordering; selected regret uses the maximum observed score minus the minimum score for the primary prediction choice
Full shared native capture, exact independent per-world controller replay and scalar observed-velocity conversion remain unchanged
Missing, crossed, duplicate or unmatched trials, excessive dispersion, nonconvergent predictions or source/runtime drift refuse the comparison
Explicit actuator-aware mode uses ordered XML-bound joint armature, clipped motor forces and saturation-aware velocity derivatives
Native CPU and packed GPU armature/damping arrays match explicit XML before stepping and during independent replay
The original predictor remains selected by v1/v2 schemas; the new schema and component digest are required for the corrected model
not_covered: Learned selection, beneficial memory or untouched body generalization
Future contact generation or multistep prediction accuracy
Weakened actuators, impacts, new initial orientations or terrain
Live Godot recovery handoff, real time, cross-engine equivalence or release
route_horizon_rationale: 165 fresh worlds in three 55-world batches: three bodies, three intervention times, nine actions and two repeats per action, plus one plain comparator per body. Every world runs 121 controller intervals and 605 native substeps. Both repeats of every action bound observed numerical dispersion at each intervention. No state reset, cached baseline, recovery cohort or statistical generalization.
qualification_economy: Reuse the same native owner, population shape, bounded nine-action family and numerical/interval reader. Thirteen focused actuator controls cover reflected inertia, implicit feedback, saturation, damping, force binding and metric reading; three route controls cover explicit dispatch, native/GPU parameter readback and versioned comparison. Existing 207 controls remain applicable.
comparison_limits: Two repeats measure finite observed dispersion only; they do not bound all stochastic variation or establish statistical confidence.
Numerically matched independently evolved worlds are not identical-state causal branches.
Prediction matching concerns the declared angular response score. Full joint predictions remain retained and replayed, with no joint-velocity accuracy claim.
The consumed v1 exact-prefix rule and refusal remain unchanged; this successor does not rescore that attempt.
The v2 valid negative remains unchanged. The actuator correction passed an exposed retained mean-error screen only; useful action ranking is the question of this new native run.
The finite inelastic friction-pyramid response model remains distinct from native elliptic soft contacts; no solver equivalence is claimed.
